answer.rationale: Constraints eliminate most options before evidence even matters: rollback_release is barred by compliance (so memory_b1 is inapplicable no matter how well it worked on day 18), and regional_failover (memory_b2) moves the write path mid-flight at settlement peak, which directly risks the 'no lost customer writes' objective — its day-33 success was a latency degradation, not a heavy-write peak, so the analogy is weak. add_capacity (memory_b3) worked as pre-provisioned headroom ahead of a known peak; provisioning during a 90-minute-old live regression is a different maneuver and likely too slow. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) fails fast on an external dependency — here the bottleneck appears internal to the write path, and failing fast on writes would shed exactly the transactions we must not lose. That leaves route_read_replicas: memory_b5 describes the closest match to the current signature — read/reporting load contending with the primary, with transactional write latency recovering once reads were shifted. It is also the only candidate that is additive rather than disruptive to in-flight writes. I want the archived source for memory_b5 to confirm the recovery was actually attributed to read offload and not confounded by a concurrent change, and whether it was applied under peak write load or in a quiet window; and memory_b3 to see whether capacity was ever added successfully mid-incident, since that is my fallback if b5's record is thinner than the consolidated summary implies. Caveat on the causal story: I have not confirmed that read contention is the driver of this latency climb — the release two hours ago is a live confounder, and if the security patch itself added write-path cost (extra crypto, added audit writes, new synchronous validation), offloading reads will not touch it. Timing is suggestive but the climb began before the release window fully aligns, so it stays unresolved. Hence small_guarded_test: shift the heaviest reporting/dashboard read cohort first and watch p99 on the write path for a defined interval, expanding only on a clear signal, so that a wrong hypothesis costs one cohort rather than the settlement window. Downstream value risk: replica lag means reads served from replicas can be stale, and if any settlement, reconciliation, balance check, or fraud decision consumes those reads, stale data could propagate into financial outcomes that look like successful writes — so reporting/analytics queries only, with anything on the authoritative transaction path pinned to the primary, and lag monitored explicitly.
